q: Which selector has the highest specificity?
t: Specificity order: inline styles, then ids, then classes and attributes, then elements.

q: With box-sizing: content-box, width 200px, padding 20px and border 5px, what is the total width?
t: content-box adds padding and border to width: 200 + 2x20 + 2x5 = 250.

q: With box-sizing: border-box, width 200px, padding 20px and border 5px, what is the total width?
t: border-box includes padding and border inside the width.

q: Which flexbox property aligns items along the main axis?
t: justify-content works on the main axis, align-items on the cross axis.

q: What does flex: 1 usually mean?
c: The item grows to share the available space
t: flex: 1 is shorthand for grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0, so items share space equally.

q: Which declaration makes a responsive grid with columns at least 200px wide that fill the row?
t: repeat(auto-fit, minmax()) creates as many columns as fit, each at least 200px.

q: What does position: sticky do?
c: Acts like relative until a scroll threshold, then sticks
w: Fixes the element to the page forever
t: Sticky elements stay in view inside their container once you scroll past a set offset.

q: Which position value places an element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor?
t: absolute removes the element from flow and positions it against the nearest ancestor with a position other than static.

q: Which unit is relative to the root element's font size?
t: rem uses the root font size. em uses the parent's font size.

q: What is the difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
c: none removes the element from layout, hidden keeps its space
w: hidden removes layout, none keeps it
t: With visibility: hidden the box still takes up space.

q: Which media query targets screens at most 600px wide?
t: max-width applies up to and including that width.

q: What is mobile-first CSS?
c: Base styles for small screens, then min-width queries for larger screens
t: Mobile-first keeps the base styles simple and adds complexity as space allows.

q: What does margin: 0 auto do to a block element with a set width?
t: Auto left and right margins split the leftover space equally.

q: What is margin collapsing?
c: Vertical margins of adjacent blocks combining into one
t: When two vertical margins touch, the larger one wins instead of adding up.

q: Which property controls the stacking order of positioned elements?
t: Higher z-index values sit on top, within the same stacking context.

q: Which pseudo-class styles a link while the pointer is over it?
t: :hover matches while the pointer is over an element. :active matches while it is being pressed.

q: What does :nth-child(2n) select?
t: 2n matches 2, 4, 6 and so on.

q: Which option hides an element from everyone, including screen readers?
t: display: none removes the element from layout and the accessibility tree.

q: Which property creates a smooth change between states, such as on hover?
t: transition animates property changes over a duration.

q: How do animations differ from transitions?
c: Animations use keyframes and can run without a state change
t: Keyframe animations can loop, run automatically and have many steps.

q: Which property is the most performance-friendly to animate?
t: transform and opacity can be handled by the GPU without recalculating layout.

q: What does the cascade decide?
c: Which rule wins when several rules target the same element
t: The order of precedence is importance, then specificity, then source order.

q: What does !important do?
c: Overrides normal specificity for that declaration
t: Overusing it makes CSS hard to maintain.

q: Which property is inherited by default?
t: Text properties like color and font-family inherit. Box properties like margin and border do not.

q: How do you use a custom property named --brand?
t: CSS variables are custom properties that can be read with var().

q: What is true about em units for font-size?
c: They are relative to the parent element's font size
w: They are relative to the root
t: em compounds when nested. rem avoids that by using the root.

q: Which declaration makes an element a flex container?
t: display: flex enables flexbox layout for the direct children.

q: What does gap do in flex or grid layouts?
t: gap is cleaner than margins because it only adds space between items.

q: Which declaration lets flex items wrap onto new lines?
t: By default flex items stay on one line and may shrink.

q: How do you make a grid item span two columns?
t: grid-column: span 2 makes the item cover two column tracks.

q: What does object-fit: cover do on an image?
c: Fills the box and crops overflow while keeping the aspect ratio
w: Shrinks the image to fit entirely
t: cover fills the box without distortion, cropping what does not fit.

q: Which combination truncates a single line of text with an ellipsis?
c: overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis
t: All three are needed: hide overflow, stop wrapping and request the ellipsis.

q: What does @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) detect?
c: Whether the user's system is set to dark mode
t: It lets your CSS follow the user's light or dark preference.

q: What does clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem) do?
c: Picks a fluid value between a minimum and a maximum
t: The value grows with 4vw but never goes below 1rem or above 2rem.

q: Which selector matches only direct children?
t: Descendant is a space, child is >, adjacent sibling is + and general sibling is ~.

q: What does the selector a[href^="https"] match?
c: Links whose href starts with https
w: Links whose href ends with https
t: ^= means starts with, $= means ends with and *= means contains.

q: Which property changes the visual order of flex items without changing the HTML?
t: order changes visual order only. Keyboard and screen reader order still follow the HTML.

q: What is :focus-visible useful for?
c: Showing focus styles mainly for keyboard users
t: It avoids showing focus rings on mouse clicks while keeping them for keyboard navigation.

q: What does line-height: 1.5 without a unit mean?
c: 1.5 times the element's own font size
t: Unitless values scale with the font size and inherit well.
